story-summary.description: Implement fast condition evaluators for different trigger types (price, portfolio, silence) that run WITHOUT LLM calls. These evaluators check if a trigger condition is met and return True/False. Only if True does the system invoke the LLM wake-up agent.
story-summary.business-value: - Fast condition checking (no LLM overhead) - Efficient polling for condition triggers - Fail-safe behavior (return False on error to prevent false alarms) - Caching to avoid rate limits (yfinance)

criterion.title: Price Evaluator
criterion.requirements: - Fetches current price via yfinance - Parses expression (e.g., "NVDA < 130") - Supports operators: <, >, <=, >= - Returns True if condition met - Caches price for 60 seconds (avoid rate limits) - Reliability handling (yfinance is unofficial scraper): * Retry with exponential backoff (3 attempts) * Fail-safe: return False on error (don't fire on error) * Log errors for monitoring

criterion.title: Portfolio Evaluator
criterion.requirements: - Fetches portfolio via get_portfolio MCP tool - Supports expressions: * any_holding_change > X% * any_holding_down > X% * total_value >= X * total_change > X% - Returns True if condition met

criterion.title: Silence Evaluator
criterion.requirements: - Checks Redis for user:{user_id}:last_activity - Compares against threshold from expression - Returns True if silence exceeded

criterion.title: Error Handling
criterion.requirements: - Returns False on evaluator failure (fail-safe, don't fire on error) - Logs error with trigger details - Does not crash worker

design-doc.key-insights: - yfinance is an UNOFFICIAL scraper with known limitations - Rate-limited and can fail during high load - Not suitable for precision alerts - Mitigations: aggressive caching, fail-safe behavior, retry with backoff - Cache prices for 60 seconds minimum - On error, skip evaluation (don't fire)

epic-doc.key-points: - LLM-driven architecture with minimal trigger types - Condition evaluators are FAST (no LLM overhead) - LLM only invoked after condition passes

pattern.name: Portfolio Access
pattern.description: PortfolioManager class shows existing portfolio access patterns: - Uses MCP client to call get_portfolio tool - Redis caching with 5-minute TTL - Graceful degradation on errors - Returns empty portfolio on failure
pattern.code-reference: async def get_portfolio(self, user_id: str, refresh_if_empty: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]: portfolio = await self.load_portfolio_from_cache(user_id) if not portfolio.get("cached") and refresh_if_empty: portfolio = await self.refresh_portfolio(user_id) return portfolio

function.name: get_evaluator
function.logic: Map condition_type to evaluator class: - "price" -> PriceEvaluator() - "portfolio" -> PortfolioEvaluator() - "silence" -> SilenceEvaluator() - unknown -> raise ValueError

price-cache.rationale: Shorter than existing stock price cache (15 min) to be more responsive for condition triggers, but still prevents rate limiting on yfinance.

error-handling-strategy.description: On ANY error during evaluation, return EvaluatorResult(met=False, details={...}). This prevents false alarms when external services fail.
error-handling-strategy.logging: Log all errors with: - Trigger type - Expression - User ID - Error message - Duration
error-handling-strategy.retry-logic: For yfinance price fetching only: - 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) - Log each attempt - Return None after all retries fail

notes.note: Start with PriceEvaluator as it's the most critical and has the most complexity (caching, retry logic, yfinance handling). Then PortfolioEvaluator, then SilenceEvaluator.

yfinance is an unofficial Yahoo Finance scraper. It can fail or be rate-limited. The architecture accepts this limitation with aggressive caching and fail-safe behavior. For production, consider switching to a paid API (Polygon.io, Alpha Vantage) if reliability becomes an issue.
Portfolio evaluator needs to call get_portfolio with include_prices=True to get current values and calculate changes. This adds ~1-2s latency but is necessary for accurate condition evaluation.
The silence evaluator depends on Story 13.8 (User Activity Tracking) to update the last_activity timestamp. Without it, silence detection won't work.
